_comment: The pre-registration of agent_architecture.md §7's last reporting rule: budget
and hyperparameters are fixed before any test run, all method debugging happens
on train, and every arm is reported on test — never 'best of'. Committed before
the registered search and before any test rollout; its sha256 travels with every
run (harness/preregistration.py), so an edit after the fact moves the hash rather
than quietly redefining what was promised. Amendments are appended to
'amendments' with their reason, never applied by rewriting a value in place.

registered_against.note: T127, the run ledger. The last commit before any test rollout exists.

baseline: The handwritten seed candidate at the pinned candidate_prompt_versions — the
evaluation root instruction plus the six tool texts, registered once and read
twice (T125), so the reference arm and the search's seed cannot drift apart.
It enters at 0.50 abstention accuracy by choice: T107 found T17a failing 3/3
on the handwritten instruction with correct reasoning and a wrong contract
encoding, and left it for the search, because the encoding lives in the
optimizable text. A candidate repairing it is measuring what the thesis claims
to measure, and this sentence exists so that improvement cannot later be read
as a baseline that was quietly weakened.
optimized: Whatever candidate the one registered search selects. Not the best of several
searches, not the best iteration by test score, not a hand-picked candidate:
the search's own selection, on the aggregated scalar, over train alone.

measurement.pairing: the identical committed cases, in file order, for every arm and every repeat

analysis.repeat_reduction: mean over the repeats per case, before any aggregation over cases
analysis.primary_estimand: the paired difference optimized - baseline, per metric, on test_seen
analysis.test_unseen_trajectory: per-template win/loss table; no accuracy and no interval
analysis.abstention: accuracy over the unanswerable cases and the false-abstention rate over the answerable ones, reported separately and never blended
analysis.exclusion: harness_error cases leave every aggregate and are counted per arm with their sources broken out; invalid_argument never excludes
analysis.parse_failure: reported apart from answer accuracy, so a candidate degrading the output format stays distinguishable from one degrading reasoning
analysis.residual_nondeterminism: NOT MEASURED under amendment 1 — one repeat cannot disagree with itself. Reported as unmeasured rather than as zero, and every arm difference in this run is therefore read without a noise floor
analysis.multiplicity: no correction across the four metrics. They are four declared quantities, not a family searched over for a winner; the interval and the noise floor carry the uncertainty and the suite is stated to detect large effects only

method_debugging: train only. Every defect the pilot and the packets found was found on train
or on the pilot's own cases; the two test splits have never been run.
reporting: Both arms on all three splits, whatever the numbers are. A repeated run is
reported as a repeat, and §7's own repeat condition is the only one that
licenses it: residual failure counts diverging between arms mean the arms
were not measured under the same conditions. Diverging newly-recorded cache
entry counts are reported and never repaired.
stopping: The measurement is complete when both arms have three repeats on all three
splits. It is not stopped early on a favourable interval, and it is not

what: and the same for the three text-to-SQL chain models, which share its endpoint.
reflection endpoint: split from the task model's onto its own base and key.
why: Infrastructure, measured rather than assumed, and none of it is a result.
saia.gwdg.de stopped serving chat completions entirely — /v1/models answers 200
in 0.1 s while /v1/chat/completions hangs past 110 s or returns an empty 500 with
x-kong-upstream-latency: 10. chat-ai.academiccloud.de serves both models but
returns empty 500s at 25–60 %, and meters 1000 requests/day/key against a measured
~13 requests per rollout — 8600 requests for this run, four to nine days across two
keys. OpenRouter serves gemma-4-31b-it reliably at $0.10/$0.34 per Mtok against a
$5 budget; the run costs about $2.6 there. The reflection model stays on free quota
because a search makes ~30 proposal calls, which fits what 8600 rollout calls do not.
Repeats fell to 1 for the same budget: three repeats of both arms on all three
splits is 1686 rollouts and about $10.60.
cost: The three repeats were the replication, so this run does not measure residual
nondeterminism at all — the quantity every arm difference was to be read against
is unmeasured, not zero. decisions.md § Replication and the LLM cache already
considered dropping replication and rejected it on exactly this ground: the error
term becomes stated rather than bounded, on a suite already limited to large
effects. That is the price, and it is paid knowingly.
The LLM response cache stays OFF regardless. With one repeat it can no longer
collapse replicates, but off is the measurement path's setting and a run that
turned it on would not be comparable with a later three-repeat run.
not_amended: The arms, the splits, the pairing, the bootstrap unit and its seed, the two gaps,
the win/loss table, the exclusion rule, the diagnostics, and the whole protocol
section. Nothing here was relaxed because of a number: no test rollout has run.

why: The registered 100 buys zero proposals, and that is arithmetic rather than a
result. MLflow passes `trainset` and no `valset`, so GEPA evaluates the seed
candidate over the whole trainset before proposing anything — len(trainset) = 100
metric calls — and each accepted candidate costs another full evaluation, with
reflection minibatches of 3 in between (gepa/api.py:328, core/engine.py). A budget
equal to the trainset size is therefore spent entirely on measuring the seed, and
the search returns it unchanged. 500 leaves 400 after the seed's evaluation: about
three accepted candidates at a full evaluation each, plus their minibatches.
Chosen on GEPA's budget accounting and the split's size, both of which are known
without running anything. No test rollout has run.
cost: About €1.0 more of task-model spend than the registered 100 would have cost, and
roughly two hours of wall clock. The budget is still a fixed, pre-registered
number and the search still gets exactly one run.
not_amended: Everything else, including the fact that this remains one search whose selection
defines the optimized arm — not the best of several.

what: measurement.splits: order changed from [train, test_seen, test_unseen] to
[test_seen, test_unseen, train]. The set is unchanged and so is everything
why: Budget ordering, decided before any test rollout and on no test number. The
registered search cost $2.76 of the $5 available, and the measurement's 562
rollouts are estimated at $1.7-2.7 against $2.24 remaining — close enough that
the run may not finish. Which split is at risk if it does not is a choice, and
the honest one is to put the splits that carry the primary estimand and the
template-overfit holdout first. Train is last because its number is a selection
score rather than an inference, and because losing it costs one of the two gaps
rather than the comparison itself.
This changes no measurement, no metric and no analysis — only which result is
missing if the money runs out, and that this was decided in advance.
cost: If the budget is exhausted during train, the train → test_seen gap cannot be
computed and is reported as not measured. The test_seen paired comparison, the
test_unseen win/loss table and the test_seen → test_unseen gap are unaffected.
